products.name: tl;dv
products.note: Meeting recorder AI; timestamped notes; EU-hosted; GDPR; consent management

reading.body:
tl;dv offers meeting recording and summarization across 30+ languages with user data kept off AI training pipelines, positioning itself as a cheaper alternative to competitors like Gong.

The product sits at the junction of three capabilities: recording, transcription, and automated note generation. The company's claim that recordings will not train its AI, combined with EU hosting and GDPR compliance, signals a choice to treat customer conversations as confidential rather than as training fuel. This matters because most meeting intelligence platforms treat content as a training asset. The partnership with Anthropic for generative features, with metadata anonymization and randomized processing, suggests tl;dv offloads AI compute while trying to maintain user privacy guarantees.

For an AI company, this approach trades a potential data moat for user trust and regulatory compliance. The free tier with no time limits requires the company to absorb hosting and transcription costs at scale. Transcription alone, across 30+ languages and millions of meetings, generates consistent computational demand. That demand sits downstream of data center capacity and power availability. EU data residency adds infrastructure constraints that a US-only platform avoids.

The data does not show revenue, user scale, or which languages consume the most compute. It also does not specify whether the company owns transcription infrastructure or licenses it. Whether the free tier and low-cost paid plans are sustainable at scale depends on factors the profile does not reveal.

profile_text.body:
tl;dv is a company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Aachen. It describes itself as an AI-powered notetaker for meetings and insights, with the name standing for "Too Long, Didn't View." According to its site, the product records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings, produces timestamped notes, and also functions as a sales coaching platform, using AI-driven call analysis so sales managers can track playbook adherence, improve objection handling, and review rep performance. It is tracked as a meeting recorder AI with timestamped notes, EU hosting, GDPR compliance, and consent management.

The site says tl;dv supports transcription in over 30 languages and dialects, including English, Spanish, German, and Japanese, and that it integrates with CRMs, ticketing systems, knowledge management platforms, and over 5000+ other tools. It offers a Free Forever plan with no time limit, and the company contrasts this with Gong, which it says requires a $5,000+ upfront investment. tl;dv states that it partners with Anthropic to deliver generative AI, that recordings and transcripts are not used to train AI, and that data is protected with end-to-end encryption, GDPR compliance, SOC 2-certified security, and storage in ISO 27001-certified data centers with AES-256 encryption. It also says the AI drafts follow-up emails and next-step tasks and can send AI-generated reports to an inbox.

The available facts record no lawsuits and no MCP server for the company.
